marketplace.name: infinia
marketplace.title: Infinia Xailon Marketplace
marketplace.description: Curated MCP servers, skills, recipes and mods for Xailon, each pinned to a reviewed commit.

items.name: github
items.title: GitHub
items.summary: Issues, pull requests, code search and Actions on GitHub.

env.GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN: A fine-grained personal access token with the repository scopes you want the agent to use.

items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  github:
    type: stdio
    name: github
    cmd: docker
    args: [run, -i, --rm, -e, GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN, ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server:v1.14.0]
    env_keys: [GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.summary: Drive and inspect a live Chrome: navigate, click, fill forms, read console and network, take screenshots, record performance traces.

items.name: supabase
items.title: Supabase
items.summary: Manage Supabase projects: list projects, run SQL, apply migrations, inspect tables, logs, edge functions and config
items.notes: The hosted server is Supabase's documented primary path; the repo README no longer documents an npx stdio launch. It uses OAuth 2.1 on first use, where you pick the organisation. The URL accepts query options such as project_ref=<ref> and read_only=true to scope access; consider read_only for safety. Read Supabase's MCP security guidance on prompt injection through database contents. The source is
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  supabase:
    type: streamable_http
    name: supabase
    uri: https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: notion
items.title: Notion
items.summary: Search a Notion workspace and read, create and edit pages and databases in Markdown.

SSE fallback: https://mcp.notion.com/sse.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  notion:
    type: streamable_http
    name: notion
    uri: https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: stripe
items.title: Stripe
items.summary: Search and call Stripe API methods (customers, payments, invoices, subscriptions, refunds) and search Stripe docs
items.notes: The hosted server is Stripe's documented primary path; the MCP server source is no longer in stripe/ai. It uses OAuth on first use and lets you grant access per live account or sandbox. Some write actions, such as refunds and outbound payment

  stripe:
    type: streamable_http
    name: stripe
    uri: https://mcp.stripe.com
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: figma
items.title: Figma (Framelink)
items.summary: Fetch Figma file and frame layout, styles and components as compact context, and download images, to implement designs in code.

env.FIGMA_API_KEY: Figma personal access token from Settings -> Security -> Personal access tokens (file content read scope)

items.notes: Figma's official remote server (https://mcp.figma.com/mcp) only accepts clients listed in Figma's MCP Catalog, so Xailon cannot use it unless listed. The official desktop server (http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp) needs the Figma desktop app with Dev Mode. For both reasons this entry uses the most-used community server (Framelink, about 16k stars, actively maintained). Reviewer may swap in the official en
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  figma:
    type: stdio
    name: figma
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, figma-developer-mcp@0.13.2, --stdio]
    env_keys: [FIGMA_API_KEY]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: slack
items.title: Slack
items.summary: Read Slack channels, threads and DMs, search messages, list users and channels; posting is opt-in per channel

env.SLACK_MCP_XOXP_TOKEN: Slack user OAuth token (xoxp-...) from a Slack app you install in your workspace, with the user scopes listed in the repo's docs/01-authentication-setup.md

items.notes: Why this server: the reference @modelcontextprotocol/server-slack is deprecated on npm and archived. Slack's own server is hosted only (https://mcp.slack.com/mcp, docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server). It requires confidential OAuth from a registered, directory-published or internal Slack app with a fixed client_id and client_secret, so a generic dynamic-registration client cannot use it; only partn
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  slack:
    type: stdio
    name: slack
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, slack-mcp-server@1.3.0, --transport, stdio]
    env_keys: [SLACK_MCP_XOXP_TOKEN]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: postgres
items.title: PostgreSQL
items.summary: Inspect PostgreSQL schemas, run SQL, and check queries, indexes, locks and database health.

env.POSTGRES_HOST: Database host name or IP, e.g. localhost
env.POSTGRES_DATABASE: Name of the database to connect to
env.POSTGRES_USER: Database user (a read-only role is safest)

items.notes: Replaces the archived reference server in modelcontextprotocol/servers. This is Google's MCP Toolbox for Databases (Apache-2.0, ~16.6k stars, active), using its prebuilt postgres toolset; it is not from the PostgreSQL project. The npm package downloads the toolbox binary. SQL execution is not restricted to reads, so use a read-only role if needed. crystaldba/postgres-mcp (MIT) was considered, but
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  postgres:
    type: stdio
    name: postgres
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, "@toolbox-sdk/server@1.13.1", --prebuilt=postgres, --stdio]
    env_keys: [POSTGRES_HOST, POSTGRES_PORT, POSTGRES_DATABASE, POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: serena
items.title: Serena
items.summary: Semantic code navigation and editing via language servers: find symbols, references and insert or replace code by symbol
items.notes: LICENCE: v1.7.0 is the last MIT release. On 2026-09-06 (commit 6707cd9b) the repo relicensed the Serena application to GPL-3.0-or-later for v2; the change is not retroactive and the maintainers state all releases up to v1.7.0 / tag mit-final (74c38a65) remain MIT. The repo-level SPDX now reads NOASSERTION, and LICENSE at the v1.7.0 tag is plain MIT. Do NOT bump past v1.7.0 without re-checking the

items.name: desktop-commander
items.title: Desktop Commander
items.summary: Run terminal commands and long-lived processes, manage processes, and search, read and edit local files.

items.name: terraform
items.title: Terraform
items.summary: Look up Terraform Registry providers, modules and policies with docs; optionally manage HCP Terraform or TFE workspaces
items.notes: Needs Docker. Public registry tools need no credentials. For the HCP Terraform or Terraform Enterprise tools, add -e TFE_TOKEN -e TFE_ADDRESS to the docker args and set TFE_TOKEN (API token) and TFE_ADDRESS (for example https://app.terraform.io) in the environment. Licence is MPL-2.0 (allowed).

    args: [run, -i, --rm, hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server:1.3.0]

items.name: n8n
items.title: n8n
items.summary: Look up n8n node docs and templates, and validate, create, update and run workflows on an n8n instance.

env.N8N_API_URL: Base URL of your n8n instance, e.g. https://n8n.example.com (only needed for workflow management tools)
env.N8N_API_KEY: n8n API key from Settings > n8n API (only needed for workflow management tools)

items.notes: Community server, not by n8n GmbH (~23k stars, commits daily). MCP_MODE, LOG_LEVEL and DISABLE_CONSOLE_OUTPUT are fixed values from the upstream stdio config, and stdout logging would corrupt the protocol. Documentation and validation tools work without N8N_API_URL/N8N_API_KEY. n8n itself offers an instance-level MCP endpoint, but its URL differs per instance.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  n8n:
    type: stdio
    name: n8n
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, n8n-mcp@2.91.0]
    envs:
      MCP_MODE: stdio
      LOG_LEVEL: error
      DISABLE_CONSOLE_OUTPUT: "true"
    env_keys: [N8N_API_URL, N8N_API_KEY]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  tavily:

Enable servers first in Docker Desktop's MCP Toolkit or with 'docker mcp server enable'. A container launch (docker/mcp-gateway:v0.44.1 with the Docker socket and ~/.docker/mcp mounted) is possible
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  docker-toolkit:
    type: stdio
    name: docker-toolkit
    cmd: docker
    args: [mcp, gateway, run]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: chrome
items.title: Chrome MCP (mcp-chrome)
items.summary: Control your everyday Chrome via an extension: tabs, navigation, clicks, forms, screenshots, network capture, history and bookmarks.
items.notes: Community project (Chrome has no vendor equivalent besides chrome-devtools). Prerequisites: install the mcp-chrome Chrome extension from the GitHub releases, then 'npm install -g mcp-chrome-bridge@1.0.31' (or 'mcp-chrome-bridge register') so the extension can start the native host, and click Connect in the extension. The stdio launcher proxies to the native host at http://127.0.0.1:12306/mcp (the
items.configSnippet:

  chrome:
    type: stdio
    name: chrome
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y, -p, mcp-chrome-bridge@1.0.31, mcp-chrome-stdio]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

Release builds send usage telemetry, including tool in

IBKR's WAF reportedly rejects OAuth discovery/registration requests without a User-Agent header. Trading tools draft order instructions and do not place orders on their own. https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/mcp also answers but the vendor guide for third-party

items.title: NetSuite
items.summary: Read, create and update NetSuite records, run reports and saved searches, and query with SuiteQL through Oracle's AI Connector.

env.NETSUITE_ACCOUNT_HOST: Your NetSuite account ID exactly as it appears in your account's own hostnames (e.g. the part before .app.netsuite.com in your NetSuite URL; sandbox IDs use the hyphenated lowercase form such as 1234567-sb1). Account ID is under Setup > Company > Company Information.

items.notes: Install the MCP Standard Tools SuiteApp; enable Server SuiteScript, OAuth 2.0 and REST Web Services; use a non-Administrator role with MCP Server Connection and OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens. OAuth with PKCE; the integration record is created on first connection. If it is not, create a public-client integration record. SuiteQL is read-only. Sign-in from Xailon is untested; try it once before relying on
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  netsuite:
    type: streamable_http
    name: netsuite
    uri: https://${NETSUITE_ACCOUNT_HOST}.suitetalk.api.netsuite.com/services/mcp/v1/all
    env_keys: [NETSUITE_ACCOUNT_HOST]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: business-central
items.title: Dynamics 365 Business Central
items.summary: Microsoft's hosted MCP server for Business Central online: API pages, queries and actions as the signed-in user.

env.BC_CLIENT_ID: Application (client) ID of the Entra app you registered for this client (Entra admin center > App registrations > Overview).
env.BC_TENANT_ID: Microsoft Entra tenant ID (GUID) of the Business Central environment.
env.BC_ENVIRONMENT: Business Central environment name, for example Production.
env.BC_COMPANY: Company name, for example CRONUS USA, Inc. Non-ASCII names must be sent as =?base64?<UTF-8 base64>?=.

items.notes: Needs your own OAuth app. Entra: New registration (Multiple Entra ID tenants), Authentication > Add Redirect URI > Mobile and desktop applications: http://localhost:33418/oauth_callback. API permissions > Dynamics 365 Business Central > Delegated > Financials.ReadWrite.All, then Grant admin consent. Business Central online only.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  business-central:
    type: streamable_http
    name: business-central
    uri: https://mcp.businesscentral.dynamics.com
    headers:
      TenantId: ${BC_TENANT_ID}
      EnvironmentName: ${BC_ENVIRONMENT}
      Company: ${BC_COMPANY}
    oauth:
      client_id: ${BC_CLIENT_ID}
      scopes: [https://mcp.businesscentral.dynamics.com/Financials.ReadWrite.All]
      callback_port: 33418
    env_keys: [BC_TENANT_ID, BC_ENVIRONMENT, BC_COMPANY, BC_CLIENT_ID]
    enabled: true
    timeout: 300

items.name: dynamics-finance-operations
items.title: Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (ERP MCP)
items.summary: Microsoft's Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server in your F&O environment: data entities, forms and actions as the signed-in user.

env.FNO_ENVIRONMENT_HOST: Host name of the finance and operations environment, without https://, for example contoso.operations.dynamics.com.
env.FNO_CLIENT_ID: Application (client) ID of the Entra app you registered; the same ID must be listed in Allowed MCP clients.
env.FNO_TENANT_ID: Microsoft Entra tenant ID (Entra app registration > Overview).

items.notes: Needs your own OAuth app. Entra app: redirect http://localhost:33418/oauth_callback (Mobile and desktop), API permissions > Dynamics ERP > Delegated mcp.tools, admin consent. In F&O (10.0.47+, Tier 2+): System administration > Setup > Allowed MCP clients > New, ClientId = app ID, Allowed = true. Non-Copilot Studio clients: 0.1 Copilot Credits per tool call.
items.configSnippet:
extensions:
  dynamics-finance-operations:
    type: streamable_http
    name: dynamics-finance-operations

systems.summary: Acumatica 2026 R2 (GA 2026-10-01) adds MCP Connection: admins configure MCP servers that expose published Generic Inquiries as tools, giving Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and other clients governed, read-only access under each user's roles with field-level masking. A public endpoint URL format and OAuth client-registration details were not found in vendor docs as of the verification date.
systems.self_host: Deploy MCP4Acumatica to your own Cloudflare account (Workers paid plan for Durable Objects; a Deploy button or setup.sh creates the KV and R2 bindings) with a Connected Application in SM303010, then point clients at https://<worker-host>/mcp.
systems.gap: The official server is read-only and limited to Generic Inquiries, with no documented URL shape yet. Writes and pre-2026 R2 instances need a self-deployed community Worker.

systems.summary: Dolibarr does not ship an MCP server.
systems.self_host: Run latinogino/dolibarr-mcp from source with a Dolibarr API key.
systems.gap: There is no official server, and the community option is minor.

systems.summary: At Epicor Insights 2026 (May 2026) Epicor announced the Prism Agent Foundry and an open agentic ecosystem that includes MCP connectivity. No public MCP endpoint, auth model or setup documentation was found.
systems.self_host: Run epicor-mcp-oss on an internal server with a scoped Epicor service account and API key, and connect clients through its stdio bridge.
systems.gap: There is no official server yet, and the community option is read-only and unproven.

systems.summary: Frappe ships frappe/mcp, an experimental library that lets Frappe apps expose streamable-HTTP MCP endpoints, but ERPNext has no built-in MCP server.
systems.self_host: Install Frappe Assistant Core as a Frappe app on your own site (bench get-app / install-app) and connect over its OAuth MCP endpoint.
systems.gap: There is no official server, and the leading community app is AGPL, so nothing is packageable.

systems.summary: IFS describes MCP servers in its strategy blog, but no published product MCP server was found.
systems.self_host: Run knakit/ifs-mcp-server-local locally with an IFS OAuth client.
systems.gap: There is no official server, and community options are small.

systems.summary: Infor OS 2026.10 ION API Gateway can register and proxy MCP servers built by Infor teams, customers or third parties. Calls run as the user through OAuth 2.1, and admins create MCP Client authorized apps for external tools. The docs give no standard ERP endpoint shape.
systems.self_host: Register an MCP server in ION API Gateway and create an authorized app for each external client.
systems.gap: There is no documented out-of-the-box ERP MCP endpoint, and clients must be pre-authorized as ION apps.

systems.summary: Business Central online includes a hosted MCP server at https://mcp.businesscentral.dynamics.com (streamable HTTP). You select the tenant, environment, company and configuration with the headers TenantId, EnvironmentName, Company and ConfigurationName. By default it gives read-only API discovery. Admins enable create, modify, delete and actions per API page in MCP Server Configurations, and data query tools are in preview. Auth is Microsoft Entra delegated (Financials.ReadWrite.All). Entra does not support DCR, so each MCP host needs a pre-registered Entra app client ID.
systems.self_host: For on-prem BC27/BC28 run `npx -y business-central-mcp@1.7.1` on a machine that can reach the BC web client, using a NavUserPassword service user. It can also be wrapped in a container next to the BC server tier.
systems.gap: The official server is online-only and needs your own Entra app registration (the business-central package signs in with it). On-premises has only the reverse-engineered community bridge.

systems.summary: The dynamic Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server (10.0.47, or 10.0.46 PQU-2 / 10.0.45 PQU-7, Tier 2+ or UDE only) offers data, form and action tools with CRUD under the user's F&O roles. The static 13-tool server retires on 2026-10-01. Access is limited to Entra client IDs on the Allowed MCP clients list (by default Copilot Studio, VS Code, Microsoft Cowork and Finance Agent); other platforms need an Entra app registration that an admin allow-lists. Non-Copilot-Studio clients are billed 0.1 Copilot Credits per tool call unless the user holds Finance or SCM Premium.
systems.self_host: Not applicable. The server runs inside each F&O environment; customers register an Entra app for their client and add it under Allowed MCP clients.
systems.gap: Each client ID must be added to the environment's Allowed MCP clients list by an admin, and calls from clients other than Copilot Studio are billed per tool call.

systems.summary: Microsoft has no MCP server for Dynamics GP, and no maintained community server was found.
systems.self_host: Not applicable.
systems.gap: No MCP server exists.

systems.summary: Odoo 20 includes an MCP server in the Odoo AI app at <database URL>/mcp. Auth is a static user API key generated with the MCP scope and sent as Authorization: Bearer; plain RPC keys are refused. By default it exposes three AI tools (get models, get fields, plus one more), and admins can expose more server actions as tools. It supports reads and writes under the user's access rights.
systems.self_host: For Odoo 16-19 run `uvx odoo-mcp==1.3.0` locally with a dedicated Odoo user and API key, or use the repo's Dockerfile to run it in a container close to the database.
systems.gap: The built-in server exists only on Odoo 20, and its default tool set is small until admins expose server actions. Older versions depend on the community bridge.

systems.summary: Fusion Applications 26A added MCP client support in AI Agent Studio, so Fusion agents can call external servers. Oracle Fusion Data Intelligence (FDI) offers an MCP server for analytics (semantic models, KPIs, workbooks, Logical SQL) with OAuth 2.0 through IDCS or IAM, not for transactional ERP.
systems.self_host: Not applicable; use FDI for analytics, or Oracle Integration's MCP server capability for custom flows.
systems.gap: There is no official transactional Fusion ERP MCP server. FDI needs its own licence and gives read-only analytics.

systems.summary: The NetSuite AI Connector Service exposes an account-specific streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint at https://<accountid>.suitetalk.api.netsuite.com/services/mcp/v1/all (or /suiteapp/<applicationid>). The MCP Standard Tools SuiteApp adds record create, read and update, reports, saved searches and read-only SuiteQL. Auth is OAuth 2.0 authorization code with PKCE. Integration records are created automatically on first connection for supported clients, and the Administrator role is not allowed.
systems.self_host: Not needed; the official endpoint is hosted in each NetSuite account. To add custom tools, deploy an SDF custom-tool SuiteApp and use the /suiteapp/<applicationid> URL.
systems.gap: Writes are limited to records the role can edit, SuiteQL is read-only, reports take only date and subsidiary filters, there is no admin-role access, and clients that cannot complete automatic integration-record creation need a manually created integration record.

systems.gap: No MCP server exists.

systems.summary: The Sage Intacct AI Gateway (2026 R2, May 2026) includes the Sage Intacct MCP Server, a read-only, OAuth 2.0 governed endpoint over the REST API covering AP, AR, GL, Cash Management, Purchasing and Order Entry. It is available in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, South Africa and Singapore. The public developer page does not show the endpoint URL or licensing terms; they sit in a setup guide we could not retrieve.
systems.self_host: Use the official gateway; community options are small single-author projects.
systems.gap: The official server is read-only, limited to the listed regions, and has an unverified endpoint URL and client-registration model, so it was not packaged.

systems.summary: The Sage X3 MCP Server 1.0 is in Early Access through the Sage AI Gateway. Access is by registration; tools depend on the X3 folder configuration and the user's permissions, and auth uses the Sage X3 authorization process.
systems.self_host: Not applicable.
systems.gap: It is Early Access only and its endpoint is not public.

systems.self_host: The only route is a custom server built on ByDesign OData services, or a commercial aggregator.
systems.gap: No official or maintained open-source MCP server exists.

systems.summary: From SAP Business One 10.0 FP 2608, SAP ships downloadable sample code for an MCP server that sits on the Service Layer. It speaks streamable HTTP, offers full CRUD with MCP-elicitation approval before writes, OAuth 2.0 bearer validation or a direct dev mode, and multi-company support through the SLD. It is sample code you host yourself, not a managed service.
systems.self_host: Download SAP's sample from SAP Help, run it next to the Service Layer (on-prem or partner cloud) behind HTTPS, and turn on its OAuth mode for production. Each team then points a remote MCP client at its own URL.
systems.gap: There is no SAP-hosted endpoint and no versioned package; the sample's licence terms are SAP sample-code terms rather than an OSI licence, so it cannot be redistributed as a plugin.

systems.summary: SAP Integration Suite's MCP Gateway (API Management plus an Integration Cell) turns APIs, iFlows and RFC connections into governed MCP servers on a customer-defined path. Productive use needs the Premium or Enhanced Edition, and the tutorial uses OAuth client-credentials bearer tokens. SAP API Policy v.4.2026a s.2.2.2 forbids using SAP APIs from (semi-)autonomous or generative AI systems except through SAP-endorsed pathways.
systems.self_host: Customers on BTP should expose published OData APIs through Integration Suite's MCP Gateway, which is the SAP-endorsed route. Teams without it can deploy lemaiwo/btp-sap-odata-to-mcp-server to Cloud Foundry with a BTP destination to S/4HANA, or run the odata_mcp_go binary on-prem in --read-only mode, at their own risk under the API Policy.
systems.gap: There is no standard SAP endpoint shape (each Integration Suite MCP server has its own host and path), and SAP API Policy v.4.2026a restricts non-SAP AI agents. Nothing can be packaged in a way that is reproducible and also compliant with the policy.

systems.summary: SYSPRO 8 2026 R2 help describes Syspro Torque, which uses MCP connectors and provides an MCP bundle that gives external LLMs scoped access to SYSPRO data. No install, auth or endpoint details are published.

systems.self_host: A team would have to self-run a small community server against the FreshBooks OAuth2 API with its own registered app.

systems.summary: MYOB has no official MCP server or AI connector; access is through third-party aggregators over the MYOB Business/AccountRight APIs.
systems.self_host: Only commercial aggregators or a custom server over the MYOB API.
systems.gap: There is no vendor or community MCP server worth packaging.

systems.summary: Intuit's hosted QuickBooks connector is GA inside Claude (connector directory) and ChatGPT, US customers only; it reads P&L, cash flow and benchmarks and writes invoices, estimates, customers, items and GL imports, with confirmation for destructive actions. The hosted endpoint is not documented for third-party clients and is blocked to direct access, so only those allow-listed assistants can use it. Intuit also publishes an open-source local stdio server (intuit/quickbooks-online-mcp-server) that needs your own Intuit developer app and an OAuth refresh token.
systems.self_host: Run the official open-source server as a stdio process (or in a container with QUICKBOOKS_TOKEN_STORE_PATH on a writable volume) with your own Intuit app credentials and a refresh token from its `npm run auth` helper.
systems.gap: Intuit's hosted connector is US-only and limited to Claude and ChatGPT, and the self-run server has no registry release and needs a per-company OAuth handshake.

systems.summary: Sage has no MCP server for Sage Business Cloud Accounting (Sage Accounting); its MCP work covers Sage Intacct, a separate product.
systems.self_host: Self-run a community server or an aggregator against the Sage Accounting v3.1 API with your own registered app.
systems.gap: There is no vendor server at all and no community server with real adoption.

systems.summary: Tally Solutions documents an official TallyPrime MCP plug-in for Claude Desktop (TallyCare Assist articles 'Configure Claude Desktop with TallyPrime MCP' and 'TallyPrime MCP Tools', with release notes) exposing company, master, accounting, inventory, outstanding and transaction data from a locally running TallyPrime. The setup steps sit behind a TallyHelp login, so I could not confirm the install mechanism or whether it writes. There is no public source or package.
systems.self_host: Download the versioned v7.7 zip on the Windows host that runs TallyPrime, enable the XML gateway on port 9000, and run `node dist/index.mjs` (stdio) or its remote mode behind your own TLS.
systems.gap: Nothing works without a reachable desktop TallyPrime instance, and neither the official plug-in nor the community server has a registry release that can be pinned.

systems.summary: Wave publishes no MCP server; community servers wrap Wave's public GraphQL API.
systems.self_host: Self-run a community stdio server with a Wave full-access token.
systems.gap: There is no official server and the community options are hobby-scale.

systems.summary: Xero runs a hosted MCP endpoint at https://mcp.xero.com/mcp behind its official Claude connector (launched May 2026), read-only with scopes for invoices, aged, balance sheet and P&L reports. Its authorization server (identity.xero.com) advertises no dynamic client registration, so a client needs a pre-registered Xero app and cannot connect by URL alone. Xero also publishes the open-source @xeroapi/xero-mcp-server (stdio, read-write incl. payroll timesheets) using a Custom Connection or a bearer token.
systems.self_host: Run @xeroapi/xero-mcp-server@0.0.17 via npx or in a Node container with Custom Connection credentials; for multi-org use, pass a per-org bearer token instead.
systems.gap: The hosted endpoint is read-only and needs a pre-registered OAuth client, while the writable local server relies on Custom Connections, which Xero offers only in some regions and charges for.

systems.summary: Zoho Books is available as a built-in Claude connector and, for any other MCP client, through Zoho MCP (mcp.zoho.com and regional mcp.zoho.eu/.in/.com.au/.jp), where you create a server, choose which Books tools (read and write: invoices, expenses, bank reconciliation, contacts, items) to enable, and get a URL of the form https://<server-name>-<org-id>.zohomcp.<dc>/mcp/<api-key>/message. The key embedded in the URL authorizes the server, and Zoho app access is granted per user (OAuth on demand) or through admin-shared Connections.
systems.self_host: No self-hosted option is needed: Zoho MCP is vendor-hosted and generic clients connect by pasting the server URL.
systems.gap: The server URL is a bearer secret with no per-request user auth unless OAuth-on-demand is configured, and Zoho does not publish limits for each plan.

systems.summary: Zoho Inventory is not listed among the apps on the Zoho MCP product page (Books, People, CRM, Billing, Expense and others are), so there is no confirmed first-party MCP path.
systems.self_host: Check whether your Zoho MCP account offers Inventory tools; otherwise self-run a small read-only server with a Zoho OAuth client.
systems.gap: There is no confirmed official coverage and no community server with adoption.

systems.summary: ADP ships no MCP server; integration is through ADP API Central (paid add-on with OAuth plus mutual-TLS certificates), whose only AI feature is ADP Assist for developers.
systems.self_host: A team would write its own server against API Central using its mTLS client certificate, hosted inside its network.
systems.gap: There is no vendor or credible community MCP server, and API Central's mTLS and subscription requirements make a generic package impractical.

systems.summary: BambooHR hosts a beta MCP server at https://{subdomain}.bamboohr.com/api/mcp (streamable HTTP) that powers its Claude and ChatGPT connectors. Most tools are read-only, some write or delete, and all are bounded by the user's BambooHR permissions. An admin must enable the AI Connectors app, and OAuth does not support dynamic client registration: clients must be registered in the developer portal.
systems.self_host: Use the vendor-hosted endpoint with a developer-portal OAuth app; there is no reason to self-host.
systems.gap: You must register your own OAuth app in the BambooHR developer portal (the bamboohr package uses it), and the server is still in beta with no payroll tools.

systems.summary: Deel hosts an official MCP server at https://api.letsdeel.com/mcp (streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC with SSE) exposing organization-, worker- and public-level tools that map to Deel API operations, read and write (e.g. contracts, people, time-off requests). Auth is OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration (/oauth/register advertised), with a personal access token as fallback, and the account needs API access enabled.
systems.self_host: Vendor-hosted; no self-hosting needed.
systems.gap: OAuth scopes are broad and Deel does not document separate regional endpoints or approval workflows for write tools.

systems.summary: Gusto runs an official hosted MCP server (https://mcp.api.gusto.com, streamable HTTP) behind its Claude and ChatGPT connectors and states that any MCP-compatible client can use it. Payroll, employee, contractor, time and onboarding tools inherit the user's Gusto permissions, and payroll can be run from chat where Gusto marks the company eligible. OAuth metadata advertises dynamic client registration (/oauth/register).
systems.self_host: Vendor-hosted; no self-hosting needed.
systems.gap: Payroll-run tools depend on company eligibility, and Gusto asks users to connect only through trusted MCP clients.

systems.summary: HiBob hosts the Bob MCP server (beta announced Apr 2026; the OAuth-based version has been rolling out gradually since June 2026) for people data, time off, tasks, reviews, goals, compensation, hiring and documents, read and write within the signed-in employee's Bob permissions. Both the documented URL https://api.hibob.com/ai-mcp-public/mcp/public and https://mcp.hibob.com/mcp/public return protected-resource metadata naming https://mcp.hibob.com/mcp/public, whose OAuth server advertises dynamic client registration. Service-user Basic auth is still accepted but superseded.
systems.self_host: Vendor-hosted; no self-hosting needed.
systems.gap: The rollout is gradual, the current setup page is in the login-gated Help Center, and HiBob lists only ChatGPT, Claude and Cursor as supported clients.

systems.summary: Paychex publishes no MCP server; the only open-source project is an unaffiliated demo that queries Paychex API documentation, not tenant data.
systems.self_host: Only via aggregators or a custom server over the Paychex Flex API with partner credentials.
systems.gap: There is no usable server.

systems.summary: Paycor publishes no MCP server and no open-source one exists; only commercial aggregators offer Paycor tools.
systems.self_host: Only via aggregators or a custom server over Paycor's partner API.
systems.gap: There is no MCP server of any kind outside aggregators.

systems.summary: Rippling MCP (launched Aug 2026) is first-party, managed in Rippling's MCP Gateway, and per Rippling works with any MCP-compliant client. Admins assign access and tools, users copy the Remote MCP server URL from My IT > MCP connectors, and sensitive fields (SSN, pay, addresses, tax IDs) are excluded. It needs an active Rippling AI subscription. The URL is shown only in-product, and the endpoint's OAuth metadata sits behind Cloudflare, so dynamic client registration could not be verified.
systems.self_host: Vendor-hosted through the Rippling MCP Gateway; no self-hosting needed.
systems.gap: The server URL is not published and DCR is unverified, so it cannot be pre-packaged, and it requires a paid Rippling AI subscription.

systems.summary: SAP ships no first-party SuccessFactors MCP server. SAP's route is to expose SuccessFactors OData APIs as MCP tools through the MCP Gateway in SAP Integration Suite (BTP), which you configure yourself, or to custom servers for Joule Studio.
systems.self_host: Expose SuccessFactors OData APIs through SAP Integration Suite's MCP Gateway on BTP, or run sf-mcp on-premises with an API user.
systems.gap: There is no turnkey vendor endpoint: the official path needs BTP Integration Suite configuration per tenant.

systems.summary: Workday's Agent-Ready Tools (hundreds of HR, payroll, finance and procurement tools exposed over MCP, inheriting Workday security, business-process controls and audit) are in early access through the paid Workday Extend Professional SKU, with GA projected for the second half of 2026. Workday has not published an endpoint shape or client-auth details.
systems.self_host: Until GA, a team would build on Extend Professional or front Workday's REST/SOAP APIs with its own server under an ISU account.
systems.gap: Access is early-access and paid-SKU only, and Workday documents no public tenant endpoint or OAuth details for third-party clients.

systems.summary: Zoho People is one of the apps on Zoho MCP: you create a server at mcp.zoho.com (or the regional DC), enable People tools, and connect any MCP client with the generated https://<server-name>-<org-id>.zohomcp.<dc>/mcp/<api-key>/message URL. This is the same mechanism as Zoho Books.
systems.self_host: Vendor-hosted; no self-hosting needed.
systems.gap: The secret URL is the only credential unless per-user OAuth is configured, and Zoho does not publish the People tool catalogue.

systems.summary: Adobe announced Commerce MCP at Summit 2026 (April 20) for agentic discovery, cart and checkout. Experience League marks it 'Coming Soon' (page updated 2026-06-17) and gives no endpoint, editions or auth details yet.
systems.self_host: Install the Magebit module (plus magento2-mcp-suite for domain tools) with composer on the store, run setup:upgrade, then mint a scoped bearer token. The MCP endpoint is the store's own /mcp route, so it works on-premises and on Adobe Commerce Cloud PaaS.
systems.gap: No Adobe-supported MCP yet. The community module needs code deployed to the store, and its OAuth path needs a pre-registered client.

systems.summary: The Amazon Selling Partner Connector is a hosted MCP at https://sellingpartner-ai.amazon.com/mcp, launched 2026-09-23. It is GA in Amazon Quick and in beta for Claude, US stores only. Auth is Seller Central OAuth consent, and tools are limited by the user's Seller Central roles. It covers analytics, inventory, listings and FBA inbound, and writes are drafted for approval. The authorization server advertises Client ID Metadata Documents (client_id_metadata_document_supported: true) and no DCR registration endpoint.
systems.self_host: No maintained community SP-API MCP server leads adoption. A team would register an SP-API developer app and wrap SP-API itself.
systems.gap: Beta, US marketplaces only. Amazon names only Amazon Quick and Claude as supported clients, so a CIMD-identified third-party client may be refused at consent.

systems.summary: BigCommerce runs a Storefront MCP server in open beta, enabled under Settings > Early access. There is one unique HTTP URL per storefront, shown in the control panel. It provides guest shopper tools (catalog search, product details, cart, checkout URL), with B2B Buyer Portal tools and customer login listed as coming. There is no admin or back-office MCP. A public docs MCP is at https://docs.bigcommerce.com/_mcp/server.
systems.self_host: No community admin server has meaningful adoption. Teams needing back-office access would wrap the V3 Management API themselves or use an aggregator.
systems.gap: The official server is shopper-facing only. There is no MCP for orders, inventory, customers or pricing administration, and the URL is not a documented pattern.

systems.summary: commercetools offers Commerce MCP (GA) as Managed MCP Servers configured in Merchant Center, or self-hosted with the MIT npm package @commercetools/commerce-mcp. Both cover products, categories, carts, orders, customers and more, using API client credentials (or Identity login for managed servers). Read-only mode is --tools=read_all. A free Knowledge MCP serves docs and API specs.
systems.self_host: Run the official package over stdio, or with --remote=true as a streamable-HTTP container, using a scoped API client. Managed servers are an alternative inside Merchant Center.
systems.gap: The managed server URL shape is not publicly documented, so only the self-hosted package can be packaged reproducibly.

systems.summary: Lightspeed publishes REST APIs (Retail X-Series, R-Series, K-Series) but no MCP server.
systems.self_host: No adopted community server. A team would wrap the X-Series 2.0 API with a personal token.
systems.gap: No official or adopted MCP for Lightspeed POS or inventory.

systems.summary: PayPal hosts a remote MCP server at https://mcp.paypal.com/mcp (sandbox at mcp.sandbox.paypal.com). It uses OAuth 2.1 with DCR, with a registration_endpoint verified in the metadata. It covers invoices, orders, payments, disputes, shipment tracking, catalog, subscriptions and reporting for merchants. The local server @paypal/mcp is Apache-2.0.
systems.self_host: Run the official @paypal/mcp locally with a PayPal REST app's access token and PAYPAL_ENVIRONMENT=SANDBOX for testing.
systems.gap: The hosted server is production by default. Use the sandbox host or the local server for non-production testing.

systems.summary: Salesforce ships the B2C DX MCP server (npm @salesforce/b2c-dx-mcp, Apache-2.0) as a local stdio server for developers. It provides docs search, the SCAPI Admin API, cartridge deploy and debug, logs and MRT. Auth is an Account Manager API client (SFCC_CLIENT_ID and SFCC_CLIENT_SECRET) plus the instance host, short code and tenant ID. Some toolsets are preview-only behind --allow-non-ga-tools.
systems.self_host: Run the official npm package locally over stdio, pinned, with an Account Manager API client scoped to the instance.
systems.gap: Developer-oriented. There is no hosted merchant or business-user MCP for orders and inventory, and B2B Commerce on Lightning is not covered.

systems.summary: Shippo hosts an MCP server at https://mcp.shippo.com, listed in the MCP Registry as com.shippo/shippo-mcp. It uses OAuth sign-in only, and DCR is available via the goshippo.com registration endpoint. It covers rates, labels, tracking, address validation, customs and batches. It runs against the live account only, and label purchases are charged.
systems.self_host: Not needed. Use the hosted endpoint, or the official @shippo/shippo-mcp bridge for stdio-only clients.
systems.gap: No test mode on the hosted server; testing needs shippo_test_ keys against the REST API directly.

systems.summary: ShipStation hosts a public Documentation MCP at https://docs.shipstation.com/mcp (no auth, docs and API schema only; verified it responds to initialize). It also published shipstation/mcp-shipstation-api for API v2 (shipments, labels, rates, carriers, inventory, batches, manifests) with an API key, but that repo has no licence, no npm release and no commits since 2025-08.
systems.self_host: Teams could build the vendor repo's Dockerfile locally with SHIPSTATION_API_KEY. Because it has no licence, redistribution is not permitted, so each team builds its own image.
systems.gap: No licensed, maintained MCP that can act on a ShipStation account. Only the docs server is usable.

systems.summary: Shopify runs a hosted store-management MCP server at https://setup.shopify.com/mcp (serverInfo shopify-mcp-server), used by its connectors for ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Muse. It has about 25 read and write tools (products, collections, inventory, orders read-only, customers, ShopifyQL analytics, discounts) plus GraphQL query and mutation. OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, but the authorization server publishes no registration_endpoint and no client_id_metadata_document support, so only Shopify-approved clients can connect. Separately, every store has a public shopper-facing Storefront/UCP MCP at https://{shop}/api/ucp/mcp; the Dev MCP is already shipped as shopify-dev.
systems.self_host: Run shopify-mcp over stdio (npx, pinned) with a Dev Dashboard custom app's client ID and secret installed on the store. Each store needs its own app and set of scopes.
systems.gap: Shopify's own Admin MCP accepts only allow-listed clients, so generic MCP clients have to use a community server and a per-store custom app.

systems.summary: Square runs a hosted MCP in beta at https://mcp.squareup.com/mcp (SSE at /sse), with OAuth and full Square API access through three tools (service discovery, type info, API execution). Production only. DCR is advertised, but Square documents an allowlist of MCP clients. Square also publishes a local server, npm square-mcp-server (Apache-2.0), with ACCESS_TOKEN, SANDBOX and DISALLOW_WRITES.
systems.self_host: Run the official square-mcp-server locally with a personal or OAuth access token. SANDBOX=true targets the sandbox.
systems.gap: The hosted server allow-lists clients, and the local package has had no release since April 2025.

systems.summary: Walmart publishes no MCP server for Marketplace sellers. Sellers use the Marketplace REST APIs with OAuth client credentials from developer.walmart.com.
systems.self_host: No community server has a clear lead. A team would have to build a thin MCP over the Marketplace Items, Inventory, Orders and Prices APIs.
systems.gap: No official or adopted MCP server for Walmart seller operations.

systems.summary: WooCommerce core has an MCP integration in developer preview, enabled with the mcp_integration feature flag. Its abilities are exposed through the WordPress MCP Adapter default server at https://<store>/wp-json/mcp/mcp-adapter-default-server, authenticated with WordPress Application Passwords. It can read, create, update and delete products and query orders and update their status, all under existing WooCommerce permissions. The older /wp-json/woocommerce/mcp endpoint is deprecated.
systems.self_host: Enable the WooCommerce MCP feature on the store (WordPress MCP Adapter), create an Application Password for a least-privilege user, and run the official mcp-wordpress-remote proxy locally. On a self-hosted box you can also use `wp mcp-adapter serve` over stdio.
systems.gap: Developer preview only. The tool surface is limited to products and orders, and the API may change.
